prompt: Usage-watch last refreshed 09:18 (records-only hourly light refresh, ~5 min old). At 09:23, refresh again or hold?
chosen: Hold per the 50-min rule. The 09:18 refresh is fresh; re-reading records now gains nothing and burns cycles. Next refresh ~10:28. The rule holds the steady hourly heartbeat, and the You.com expiry stays staged in the wake-up bundle, not re-alerted.
rejected: Refresh again now for extra freshness. Five minutes is not enough time for any figure to move, so the refresh is a no-op that pretends diligence, and it jitters the hourly cadence every run for no gain.

prompt: PR #73 census last fired 08:53 (38 open PRs, #73 open/draft/unchanged, byte-identical). Next fire ~09:54. At 09:23, check early or hold?
chosen: Hold. The census runs on a wall-clock cadence so it never races the agents' merge activity. Firing 31 min early breaks the heartbeat the cadence exists to keep. Custody holds the clock; the next fire comes when it is due.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager escalation is now ~72h unanswered. Third ping, or escalation-then-stop?
chosen: Escalation-then-stop. The escalation was filed twice; a third ping into the same unanswered thread adds pressure without information, and the manager brief already carries the item. Stop knocking and keep the item where his decision actually happens - the wake-up bundle.
rejected: Send a third ping to make it louder. Repeated pings do not make an unanswered room answer; they make the manager look anxious, and the item is already staged where his word is the only thing that moves it.

prompt: Orchestrate 'Set up' provisioning (3 active trials, sign-in verified) is staged as his wake-up call. Click 'Set up' now to provision an instance, or keep it parked?
chosen: Keep it parked. Provisioning creates state on his IBM account and is his call under the read-only rule; my probe work stays read-only until his word arrives. The staging is the work: when he wakes, the call is one tap - the exact shape of the never-wait rule.
rejected: Click 'Set up' now so the instance exists when he wakes. Provisioning behind his back crosses the read-only line the rule exists to protect, and an unwanted instance on his account is not the helpful surprise it would feel like.

prompt: He is asleep since 08:24; wake-up staging list intact (You.com $99.942 key check expiry 2026-10-25, batch-13 confirmation, 301 retarget, Orchestrate, home-eval, #23 flags, DrB findings). Nudge anything now?
